record.original_question: Let E_lambda(u) denote the energy functional for the Brezis-Nirenberg problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega subset of R^3 with u = 0 on partial Omega. If a family u_lambda is said to blow up with finite energy at a fixed parameter value lambdabar when ||u_lambda||_{L^infty(Omega)} -> +infinity and E_lambda(u_lambda) remains bounded as lambda -> lambdabar, can one construct such finite-energy blow-up solutions when the fixed concentration value differs from the positive threshold lambda* identified by Druet, possibly assuming Omega is convex?

evidence.quote: We say that u_lambda is a blow-up solution of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) with finite energy at a fixed parameter lambda if ||u_lambda||_{L^infty(Omega)} -> +infinity and E_lambda(u_lambda) <= 1 as lambda -> lambdabar, where E_lambda(u) is the energy functional of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1).

Open question 5: In a general bounded domain Omega, if necessary, it could be convex, is it possible to construct blow-up solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) with finite energy at a fixed parameter which is different from lambda* predicted by Druet in [25] in dimension N = 3?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded smooth domain (which may be assumed convex if needed). Consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$-\Delta u = \lambda u + |u|^{2^*-2}u \ \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u=0 \ \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
where $2^* = 6$ is the critical Sobolev exponent in dimension three. The associated energy functional is
$$E_\lambda(u) = \frac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx - \frac{\lambda}{2}\int_\Omega u^2\,dx - \frac{1}{6}\int_\Omega |u|^6\,dx.$$
A family $\{u_\lambda\}$ of solutions is said to blow up with finite energy at a fixed parameter $\bar\lambda \in (0,\lambda_1(\Omega))$ if
$$\|u_\lambda\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \to +\infty \quad \text{and} \quad E_\lambda(u_\lambda) \text{ remains bounded as } \lambda \to \bar\lambda.$$
Druet has identified a specific threshold value $\lambda^*=\lambda^*(\Omega) \in (0,\lambda_1(\Omega))$ at which finite-energy single blow-up can occur in dimension three.

Question: Does there exist a bounded smooth domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (possibly required to be convex) and a value $\bar\lambda \neq \lambda^*(\Omega)$ for which one can construct a family of solutions $u_\lambda$ to the Brezis–Nirenberg problem above that blows up with finite energy at $\bar\lambda$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (König–Laurain on multibubble blow-up analysis in 3D, and 2025 papers on least-energy solutions in the non-coercive case) study finite-energy blow-up in 3D Brezis–Nirenberg, but blow-up is shown to occur at the Druet value $\lambda^*$ under various assumptions; no construction at a parameter different from $\lambda^*$ in a convex or general bounded 3D domain has been reported. The question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Multibubble blow-up analysis for the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in three dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: In dimension 3, the blow-up points must be isolated; the case of one blow-up point was treated by Druet, and multiple blow-up points were treated by König and Laurain.
status_evidence.claim: Existing constructions/analyses align finite-energy blow-up with Druet's value $\lambda^*$.

status_evidence.title: Least-energy solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in the non-coercive case in dimension 3
status_evidence.snippet: Studies least-energy solutions in 3D, related to the Druet threshold.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to focus on the Druet threshold; no construction at $\bar\lambda \neq \lambda^*$ is reported.
